active_paradigms.idea: Recover and solve the full active-contact KKT system at high precision with mpmath.findroot
active_paradigms.description: The effective current program first solves the correct epigraph NLP with SLSQP and then attempts an antipodal least-squares contact fit; the large soft-minimum/annealing block after the first return is unreachable. Its score indicates that SLSQP has probably found the correct contact topology, but its limiting accuracy is governed by finite-difference-like active-set decisions, double precision, and a least-squares polish that does not impose stationarity or all inactive inequalities. From the returned incumbent, identify short edges and diameter edges using a substantially wider diagnostic tolerance, then build the exact equality/KKT system for that fixed graph. Include coordinates with translation and rotation gauges, the squared minimum distance t, multipliers for active lower and upper constraints, stationarity equations, and normalization fixing the diameter to one. Solve this square system offline using mpmath.findroot at roughly 80-150 decimal digits, trying only contact graphs that are stable under several SLSQP reruns. Evaluate every recovered solution using all 91 distances, reject one if any nominally inactive edge violates [t,1], and embed only the best high-precision coordinates as decimal constants in the submitted function. This is a precision-and-certification route rather than another heuristic search, and can turn a tiny feasibility/contact imbalance into a reproducible score gain.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole target is the evaluator's q_min/q_max = (dmin/dmax)^2. In particular, remove the approximately 1e-5-level loss caused by an imperfect contact realization while preserving every noncontact inequality.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not solve merely the short/long distance equations as the present least-squares stage does: such a system can have flexible branches and can lower the true all-pairs minimum. The KKT multiplier signs and complementarity must be checked, and exact final returned coordinates should be rescaled from their measured maximum squared distance. mpmath work should be performed offline during construction; evaluation should return a fixed finite numpy array immediately.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on a low-dimensional symmetry-breaking deformation family
active_paradigms.description: Use a single scipy.optimize.differential_evolution call to test whether the apparent rhombic-dodecahedral/antipodal basin is globally optimal, rather than repeatedly perturbing it with local SLSQP starts. Parameterize configurations as the current best centered configuration plus a carefully selected 8-16 dimensional set of deformation modes: eigenmodes of its active-contact rigidity matrix with rigid motions removed are particularly useful. For each parameter vector, reconstruct all 14 points, center them, normalize by their actual largest pairwise squared distance, and return the exact negative value of min(q)/max(q) as the objective. Include both antipodal-breaking modes and modes that preserve antipodality, because the current final polish assumes a greedy opposite pairing and can exclude the superior topology. Bound each mode tightly enough that the family remains near the high-quality basin, for example with displacements initially limited to a few percent of the diameter, but include several larger modes to permit a contact-graph switch. Use deterministic seed, workers=1, updating='immediate', polish=False, and a population sized for the reduced dimension rather than attempting a 39-dimensional global search. If this discovers an improved topology, its best individual can itself be returned as fixed coordinates or used offline to infer a new exact contact system.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current local active-set basin and improve the exact squared ratio, especially by discovering a non-antipodal configuration or a different set of diameter contacts.
active_paradigms.cautions: Differential evolution directly in all coordinate variables is unlikely to finish within timeout and spends most evaluations on translation, rotation, and scale equivalents. Do not use a soft min/max surrogate: evaluate the exact 91 squared distances because a very narrow contact switch determines the score. Since only one optimization call is proposed, retain the incumbent as an explicit member of the deformation family so the method cannot return an obviously inferior geometry.

active_paradigms.idea: Enumerate geometric contact topologies using scipy.spatial.ConvexHull and perform a rigidity-rank filter before any coordinate fitting
active_paradigms.description: Treat the problem primarily as a finite contact-graph identification problem rather than as unconstrained coordinate optimization. For each high-scoring incumbent produced from deterministic perturbations, call scipy.spatial.ConvexHull on the centered points and classify candidate diameter pairs, hull adjacency, and short-distance contacts; retain only graph patterns that recur across independently converged solutions. Construct the active constraint Jacobian for each retained short/diameter graph and compute its rank after removing the six Euclidean rigid-motion degrees of freedom and scale. A graph with an unexpected infinitesimal flex is a strong explanation for why the current narrow least-squares contact fit drifts or fails to improve, whereas an isostatic or overconstrained graph is suitable for an exact algebraic reconstruction. Use the resulting discrete topology to select a symmetry ansatz only when that symmetry is actually supported by the graph, rather than greedily pairing nearly opposite points as the current program does. This can reveal that the seven-antipodal-orbit restriction is excluding a small symmetry-breaking gain, or conversely provide a defensible exact graph for a fixed-coordinate solution. The submitted routine need not run this analysis: its practical result is a better precomputed set of 14 coordinates with verified all-pair distances.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Increase the primary ratio by avoiding the wrong active graph and avoid numerical losses from fitting an underdetermined or inconsistent subset of contacts.
active_paradigms.cautions: Hull edges are not automatically minimum-distance edges, and diameter pairs need not be hull edges in a degenerate numerical representation, so all 91 distances remain the final authority. Perturb or use explicit tolerance handling when coplanar hull facets cause Qhull ambiguity. This is a structural discovery/certification method, not a replacement objective; any final candidate must be rescored with q.min()/q.max() exactly as the evaluator does.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the true max-min distance formulation directly with constrained SLSQP rather than soft extrema plus random contact moves.
tried_paradigms.description: The current program starts from the highly relevant rhombic-dodecahedral configuration (six axial and eight cubic vertices), then performs soft-min/soft-max gradient ascent and a long stochastic anneal over the nonsmooth exact ratio. Its strength is that this seed has the right broad symmetry and its active-set moves can escape one-coordinate traps, explaining the score near 0.991. Its principal weakness is that the soft surrogate changes the objective and its annealing has no mechanism to enforce all shortest and diameter constraints simultaneously at convergence. Parameterize 14 centered points, fixing translation by removing one coordinate block or adding centroid equalities, and add scalar t. Maximize t subject to every squared pair distance being at least t and at most 1; this is exactly the evaluator's squared ratio after scale normalization. Call scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' once from the rhombic-dodecahedral seed, using analytic Jacobians for every pairwise constraint and the objective -t. Break rotational gauge freedom by fixing a few coordinates or use a very small quadratic gauge regularizer only on redundant degrees of freedom. Set ftol near 1e-12 and a large maxiter, then return the optimized coordinates scaled arbitrarily. This attacks the actual bottleneck: coordinated satisfaction of all active short and long contacts, rather than accepting transient noisy improvements in the ratio.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize evaluator min_max_ratio = t under max squared distance normalized to 1; combined_score increases proportionally.
tried_paradigms.cautions: SLSQP needs a feasible or nearly feasible starting point, so initially scale the seed to make its largest squared distance exactly 1 and initialize t slightly below its smallest squared distance. Supply constraints with the sign convention required by SLSQP and protect against finite-difference noise by providing analytic derivatives. Do not optimize a smoothed ratio; the scalar constrained epigraph form is materially better conditioned near tied contacts. Eliminate translation and preferably rotation gauges, otherwise the constraint Jacobian is rank-deficient and SLSQP may report misleading convergence.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a deterministic contact-graph rigidity solve with nonlinear least squares, based on the active edges identified in the rhombic-dodecahedral seed.
tried_paradigms.description: The present search repeatedly discovers that only near-minimum and near-maximum pairs matter, but it samples which vertices to move rather than explicitly solving the contact equations. Extract the seed's two distance classes: candidate shortest contacts and candidate diameter contacts, and formulate residuals saying each short-contact squared distance equals t and each diameter-contact squared distance equals 1. Include centroid and orientation gauge residuals, and treat t as an additional unknown. Call scipy.optimize.least_squares on this single residual system with method='trf', tight tolerances, and an analytic sparse Jacobian whose rows touch only the two endpoints of each contact. A successful solve finds the locally rigid realization implied by the contact graph, which can reveal a symmetry-broken arrangement that the soft objective obscures. Select the contact graph from a narrowly perturbed best seed or from the exact seed, but retain only graphs for which the residual/Jacobian has the expected rank after gauge fixing. The resulting configuration should then be evaluated against all 91 pairs; its non-contact distances must remain strictly between t and 1. This is fundamentally different from random optimization because it exploits the likely fact that an optimum is characterized by a balanced, isostatic set of equal-distance constraints.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Equalize the genuinely binding minimum and maximum distance classes, reducing the slack and imbalance that leave the current score about 0.9% below the reference ratio.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Least squares alone does not enforce inequalities for non-contact pairs, so reject a solved contact graph if any omitted pair becomes shorter than t or longer than 1. Avoid imposing every seed contact blindly: an overdetermined incompatible graph can lock the solution at the original symmetric point. Gauge constraints must remove exactly translation and rotation freedom without artificially fixing a meaningful deformation. The residuals should be in squared-distance units, consistent with the evaluator's squared objective.

tried_paradigms.idea: Apply basin-hopping on the exact nonsmooth ratio with a geometry-aware coordinate parameterization and deterministic local acceptance.
tried_paradigms.description: The current code is already an ad hoc annealer, but its local proposal radii are adapted from individual accept/reject events and its soft-ascent stage can enter a basin unrelated to the exact objective. Replace that custom stochastic process with scipy.optimize.basinhopping acting directly on negative min(q)/max(q), where q are all 91 squared distances. Use a centered 39-degree-of-freedom parameterization and normalize every proposed configuration by its current maximum squared distance, so the objective becomes simply the minimum squared distance and has no scale drift. Seed basin-hopping at several fixed, reproducible perturbations of the rhombic-dodecahedral arrangement, retaining the best result deterministically; the library call's local minimizer should work on the exact piecewise-smooth objective, not the current soft proxy. Supply a custom bounded random displacement that perturbs all vertices in a correlated low-rank mode as well as independent modes, because the current active-vertex-only moves can miss collective symmetry-breaking deformations. Use a low temperature and step size comparable to the observed contact-breaking scale, with a fixed seed and enough iterations to cross narrow ridges. The notable improvement opportunity is objective fidelity: every accept/reject and local descent decision is judged by precisely the score evaluated externally. Unlike constrained SLSQP, this method is specifically intended to search competing contact graphs and can find a better basin before final exact local settling.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current rhombic-dodecahedral contact basin while optimizing only the exact squared distance ratio used in combined_score.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The default local minimizer is poorly suited to raw min/max kinks; use a local method tolerant of finite differences and ensure normalization is performed inside the objective without mutating the optimizer's input. Translation must be removed after each proposal, and a degenerate point set must return a large finite penalty rather than NaN. Basin-hopping can be expensive, so use fixed seeds and a modest number of well-scaled runs rather than the current extremely long two-level random loop. It is a global search method, not a proof of optimality; always preserve the unperturbed symmetric seed as a fallback.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the repeated local SLSQP restarts with one globally constrained differential-evolution solve of the exact epigraph problem
tried_paradigms.description: The live portion of the current program is a constrained SLSQP multistart solver: it starts from the 6 axial plus 8 cube-corner configuration, enforces a centroid and rotation gauge, and maximizes t under t <= squared distance <= 1. Its major strength is that it optimizes the evaluator's actual squared ratio with analytic constraint Jacobians; its weakness is that every start is in a narrow neighborhood of the same rhombic-dodecahedral basin and SLSQP cannot cross a contact-graph transition. Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on the 36 free coordinates plus t, with scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint representing all 182 epigraph inequalities. Retain centroid elimination and scale/gauge conventions, but give coordinate bounds broad enough to include all diameter-one configurations, for example symmetric bounds around zero after fixing the centroid. Use the exact objective -t rather than a soft min/max surrogate, set a fixed seed, use Sobol initialization, and enable polishing only if it remains part of the same differential_evolution call. Differential evolution can replace whole correlated groups of coordinates in one generation, making it materially more likely to discover a different diameter/contact graph than the current small Gaussian perturbations. Return the candidate only after explicitly rescaling by its measured maximum pairwise distance, because tiny feasibility tolerances otherwise alter the evaluated ratio.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact primary quantity t = min squared pair distance after imposing max squared pair distance <= 1; combined_score is simply t multiplied by 4.165849767.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A full 37-variable population is expensive, so use vectorized objective/constraint evaluation and a modest but meaningful population budget rather than the current many SLSQP calls. Differential evolution's default constraint handling may return a nearly feasible point; always evaluate actual pairwise distances and retain the best genuinely finite candidate. Do not optimize dmin/dmax rather than t when the diameter constraint is present, since that worsens numerical conditioning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a contact-graph least-squares solve on a symmetry-reduced 14-point packing ansatz rather than searching all coordinates independently
tried_paradigms.description: The score only exceeds the reference by about 1.6e-5, which strongly suggests that the current SLSQP solution has reached a nearly rigid extremal contact graph and that remaining losses are mostly from wrong active-set selection or numerical unequal contacts. The current program's dead code after its first return never runs, so its advertised soft-min annealing and active-set perturbation mechanism contribute nothing; only the local epigraph solves matter. Build a low-dimensional geometric ansatz from the observed near-optimal configuration by pairing points under a candidate reflection or half-turn symmetry and representing each orbit by its independent coordinates. Encode the presumed shortest edges as residuals ||pi-pj||^2-t and the presumed diameter pairs as residuals ||pi-pj||^2-1, adding centroid and gauge residuals only if not eliminated analytically. Call scipy.optimize.least_squares once with very tight tolerances to solve this overdetermined contact system, including t as a variable. This is fundamentally different from objective optimization: it seeks the algebraic intersection that makes all limiting contacts exactly equal, often yielding a substantially cleaner candidate than SLSQP's inequality-tolerance solution. Evaluate all non-contact pairs afterward and accept the construction only if every one lies in [t,1] up to a conservative tolerance; otherwise the assumed graph is invalid and should not be returned.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical and geometric tightening of the bottleneck shortest and diameter contacts, with the goal of increasing the measured min squared distance after exact diameter normalization.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The contact graph must be inferred from a high-quality incumbent using a narrow relative active band, but do not blindly include every nearly active pair because an overdetermined inconsistent graph will force t downward. Equality fitting alone does not enforce all inactive inequalities, so the final all-pairs verification is essential. Use an ansatz with only defensible symmetry, such as a single involution, rather than forcing the original full octahedral symmetry, whose raw seed is far from the reported ratio.

tried_paradigms.idea: Run deterministic basin hopping on a scale-normalized nonsmooth exact ratio to seek a new contact topology
tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.optimize.basinhopping once on an unconstrained coordinate representation in which each trial configuration is centered and divided by its actual diameter before scoring. The scalar objective should be the negative exact evaluated quantity min(q)/max(q), not the current unreachable soft-min objective, so acceptance is aligned with the evaluator at every hop. Start from the current geometric seed or a fixed reproducible perturbation of it, remove translation analytically, and optionally retain a three-coordinate rotation gauge to prevent wasted directions. Supply a custom proposal step that moves several vertices coherently rather than one coordinate at a time; this directly targets the weakness of local SLSQP, namely that switching a shortest-edge or diameter-edge set requires coordinated motion through temporarily inferior states. Let basin_hopping manage uphill Metropolis acceptance with a fixed seed and use its single local minimizer configuration to settle each proposed basin. Unlike differential evolution, this searches through a sequence of locally optimized basins and is especially suitable if the reference arrangement is separated by narrow ridges rather than a broad global basin. Track the best exact raw ratio encountered by the objective and return its normalized coordinates, not merely the last basin-hopping state.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Discovery of a contact graph with a strictly larger exact min(q)/max(q), which simultaneously raises min_max_ratio and combined_score.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The local minimizer used internally must have a fixed, small evaluation budget or total runtime can become excessive. Diameter normalization has nondifferentiable changes when the farthest pair switches, so derivative-based local settings should be avoided or treated as optional; a derivative-free local method is safer. Prevent degenerate configurations by returning a large finite penalty whenever the measured diameter is near zero or any coordinate is non-finite.
